description: Tutorial missions (concept §9). Scripted 1:1 crises on the seed/replay infrastructure: a tutorial names a seed, a mission key and a vehicle, and the machinery that makes a replay reproducible makes the lesson reproducible too. The crisis is not staged — it is a real draw that happens to be the same one every time, which is why the tutorial can talk about it in advance without lying.

tutorials.title: The Count
tutorials.summary: Get a vehicle off the pad.

steps.text: Six switches, one poll. Throw them with Q W E R T, or click. Nothing launches until every station reads GO.
All stations GO. Press Enter to arm. The terminal count runs itself from there — the switches freeze the moment it starts.
Airborne. Ascent takes ten minutes of sim time; + and - change the warp, Space pauses. The physics do not care which you pick.
Main engine cut-off. Watch the orbit close on the map. This flight was a quiet one — most are not.

tutorials.title: One Reading
tutorials.summary: A single anomaly, and the cost of knowing.

steps.text: Same drill: switches, arm, launch. Something will go wrong at about T+35. Let it.
The game paused itself. One reading is in, and two causes explain it — the candidate bars are the priors, not the answer. The clock at the top is how long you have.
Buy a diagnosis with Q or W. Each one costs seconds and channels. Waiting for the next reading is free and slower: that trade is the whole game.
Resolved. The post-mortem will show what you paid and what it told you.
The same flight, and the same fault at T+35 — the seed guarantees it. This time do not diagnose.
Act without certainty: raise the tank pressure. It is a reasonable guess against a pressure drop, and it is the wrong one here.
Raising pressure on a leak made the leak worse. A second crisis, a shorter window, and this one only takes an abort. Wrong measures are not merely wasted time.
